runs.concept: Unbuffered output: each small write goes straight to the underlying file or stream instead of through a buffer (system calls and buffered I/O under the row's locators CC25 and PoP7).
runs.claim: "Unless prompt output is required, it is advisable to wrap a BufferedWriter around any Writer whose write() operations may be costly, such as FileWriters and OutputStreamWriters." / "Without buffering, each invocation of a print() method would cause characters to be converted into bytes that would then be written immediately to the file, which can be very inefficient."

runs.concept: Growing an array: a hand-grown buffer grows its capacity in proportion to its size, not by a fixed increment (PoP2, growing arrays). PRF-17 reaches only a copy made on every append, not growth by a constant step.

runs.claim: "This over-allocates proportional to the list size, making room for additional growth.  The over-allocation is mild, but is enough to give linear-time amortized behavior over a long sequence of appends() in the presence of a poorly-performing system realloc()."

runs.concept: A hash function a type defines for its use as a key sends many keys to the same value, for example a constant or a hash of one field (PoP2, hash tables). runs.claim: "Note that using many keys with the same {@code hashCode()} is a sure way to slow down performance of any hash table."

runs.concept: Circuit breaking: after repeated failures, calls to the failing resource stop and fail at once until a trial call succeeds
runs.source_path: MicrosoftDocs/architecture-center docs/patterns/retry-content.md (Retry pattern, the paragraph that links the Circuit Breaker pattern)
runs.claim: If a request still fails after a significant number of retries, it's better for the application to prevent further requests going to the same resource and report a failure immediately. When the period expires, the application can tentatively allow one or more requests through to see whether they're successful.
